The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the emotional arc of the narrative. The author slows down time during the first two-thirds of the story to detail a single overnight visit in June. This deliberate pacing allows the reader to absorb the quiet rhythms, humor, and subtle vulnerabilities of the mother-child dynamic through small errands and domestic chores. 

Then, the author effectively uses time compression to bridge the gap to the climax, condensing three weeks of ordinary phone calls into a single short paragraph ("For three weeks, our conversations were ordinary..."). This compression mirrors how time passes when the narrator is away from their mother, making the suddenness of the July phone call and the hospital visit feel jarring and impactful. Finally, the pacing slows down once more as the narrator returns to the empty house, stretching the quiet, solitary moments of discovering the sprouted potatoes and the untouched ice trays to maximize the emotional resonance of the ending.
